Hi Chris, here's the full rundown after a day of digging.

It turned out to be more than the fake admin users we spotted last night. There was also a hidden admin account buried in the database, along with around 470 casino spam pages published under it. Code planted inside one of your plugins was keeping all of it invisible, and it was also messing with the site's caching, which is why pages were taking 15+ seconds to load for visitors.

Everything is cleaned up now. About 7 hours all in today:
\- Removed the hidden admin account and all ~470 spam pages
\- Swapped the tampered plugin for a fresh official copy
\- Reinstalled WordPress itself
\- Worked with WP Engine to reset the site's credentials and keys, and I've requested a full platform-level malware scan for independent confirmation
\- Set up Wordfence as a security scanner that will alert us if anything suspicious happens again

The result: pages now load in under 2 seconds instead of 16, and I'm keeping an eye on things for the next couple of days to make sure it stays clean.

A few things I need from you:
1\. The security reset logged everyone out of WordPress. When you log back in, set a new password, and have any other admins do the same
2\. Change your WP Engine password too, just to be safe
3\. Add me to your Google Search Console so I can get the spam pages out of Google before they hurt your rankings. Settings > Users and permissions > Add user > Full access, using this email: ken@nexxdigital.my
4\. Send a quick test through your contact form and make sure the email comes through, just to confirm your leads are still flowing after all the changes

Still on my list:
\- Search Console cleanup once I'm in
\- Update your outdated plugins (probably how they got in originally)
\- Share WP Engine's scan results when they come back

Happy to answer any questions, and I can send over a proper written report if you'd like one for your records.
